text:
Sam H: Heads-up — after the tf-module bump to v2.3.0 the canary cluster plan shows a KMS ARN change and a downstream GPU pool drift. Not safe to apply right now.
Maria L: ugh, screenshot or plan snippet?
Sam H: pastebin with plan: https://paste.redwood/s/abc123 (trimmed)
Sam H: ```~ aws_kms_key.data (aws_kms_key will be replaced)
~ resource "aws_kms_key" "data" {
    - arn = "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/old" -> (known after apply)
    + arn = "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/new" -> (known after apply)
  }
```
Quinn P: The TF module changed kms_key_id from string -> object in v2.3.0? That would create a new resource instead of reusing the old. See module inputs in registry.
Lee C: Also seeing flux reconcile failures on the same cluster, gitops-operator shows "resource conflict: attempted to create aws_kms_key that already exists" so the operator keeps trying and hitting IAM rate limits.
Maria L: Can we pin the module to v2.2.1 for the canary until we figure migration? quick revert in gitops overlay should stop churn.
Sam H: Agree. Reverted overlay to module = "redwood/gpups-kms-module/2.2.1" in the canary overlay, opened PR: https://git.redwood/ops/infra/merge/321
Quinn P: If we need to move forward with v2.3.0, safe path is:
  1) create explicit import of old KMS into new module shape or
  2) add lifecycle { ignore_changes = ["arn"] } on the module wrapper to avoid replace, or
  3) run a one-off state mv/state replace to match the new resource id
Note: option 2 is lowest risk but hides drift.
Lee C: For (2) an example wrapper fix: ```hcl
module "kms_wrapper" {
  source = "redwood/kms-wrapper"
  kms_key_id = module.kms.kms_key_id
  lifecycle = {
    ignore_changes = [kms_key_id]
  }
}
```
Maria L: Also the GPU autoscaler used that KMS key for node bootstrap secrets. If the KMS flip happens, a subset of newly provisioned GPU nodes fail to decrypt user-data and won't join. We saw ~12% pod eviction in the canary over the last hour. Cost/risk there.
deploy-bot: CI: terraform plan (canary) failed — drift detected on aws_kms_key.data, job #5421 — https://ci.redwood/5421 
Sam H: I'll keep canary pinned and schedule a maintenance window to coordinate a controlled migration: import key -> update module -> flux reconcile -> small-canary scale test.
Quinn P: One more suggestion: add a pre-reconcile check in our gitops pipeline that runs `terraform plan -out=plan` and blocks PRs that change kms_key.* replacement. Can add an allowlist for intentional key rotations.
Maria L: +1. I'll draft the gating rule and the small playbook for state-moves.
Lee C: Thanks — unblocking for now. We'll watch metrics. :eyes:
